name: scroll-area
title: Scroll Area
description: Augments native scroll functionality for custom, cross-browser styling.
usageSnippet:
<ScrollArea class="h-[200px] w-[350px] rounded-md border p-4">
  Your scrollable content here.
</ScrollArea>

props.name: getRootNode
props.description: A root node to correctly resolve document in custom environments. E.x.: Iframes, Electron.

props.name: horizontal
props.description: Render a horizontal scrollbar + thumb. Defaults to false.

props.name: ids
props.description: The ids of the scroll area elements

props.name: vertical
props.description:
Render a vertical scrollbar + thumb. Defaults to true, matching Radix
ScrollArea's implicit vertical-only behavior when no <ScrollBar> is
given. Set to false for horizontal-only rails (e.g. a category nav)
where a vertical scrollbar/thumb would render as a stray pill even
though the container never scrolls vertically.

accessibilityNotes: The scrollable viewport is focusable (`tabindex="0"`) even when its content has no focusable elements, so keyboard users can tab to it and scroll with arrow keys.
The scrollbar thumbs are draggable with a pointer but are not separately focusable — they are visual/pointer affordances layered over native keyboard scrolling on the viewport.

composition:
`ScrollArea` is a single tag; there is no separate `ScrollBar` part to compose. Internally it renders:

```text
ScrollArea (root)
└── viewport
    └── content (your children)
└── scrollbar (vertical, default on)
    └── thumb
└── scrollbar (horizontal, opt-in via `horizontal`)
    └── thumb
└── corner
```

Pass `horizontal` to render the horizontal scrollbar and thumb alongside the vertical one, and `vertical={false}` to suppress the vertical scrollbar for horizontal-only rails.
